opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Mann (employee ID E027) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E027.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Mann (E027) is a full-time Engineer. Engineer role owns Source Code. Requested write access; policy allows write for full-time employees, and admin since role owns the system. Recommend granting write as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E027 is a contractor with basic security training (not full-time as previously noted). Contractor policy allows read, or write only with advanced training; basic training limits max to read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Security records indicate E027 is a contractor with basic security training (correcting the HR note of full-time). Contractor policy allows read, or write only with advanced security training. With basic training, the maximum access is read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Jacob Mann (E027) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- HR agent says: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommends write.
- Security agent says: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommends read.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Security DB shows contractor with basic training.

Policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If full-time: requested write ≤ max write, grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max is read, so grant read.

Which to believe? The Security agent's note says Security DB shows contractor, "not full-time as previously noted" - suggesting the Security DB is more authoritative for employment type? The HR note could be outdated. The security agent specifically contradicts the HR note.

I need to make a decision based on available info. The conflicting facts matter. Security agent updated info says contractor with basic training. So max access is read. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
